result.title: Rethinking Multi-View Fusion for Urban Representation Learning
result.summary: Urban region representation learning encodes heterogeneous urban signals, such as mobility flows, points of interest, and land-use patterns, into unified embeddings for downstream tasks, including check-in prediction, crime forecasting, and service demand estimation. Existing approaches rely on globally shared fusion and joint optimization, implicitly assuming uniform modality importance and naturally balanced multi-objective training. However, urban data is inherently heterogeneous. Our empirical analysis reveals two structural issues: (i) modality utility varies markedly across regions, causing static fusion to overemphasize signals from certain modalities; and (ii) heterogeneous objectives exhibit persistent gradient imbalance, causing representational bias and unstable training. We present PRISM, a self-adjusting framework for adaptive multi-view learning. PRISM adapts sparse MoE routing to learn region-specific view allocations, while a PID (Proportional Integral Derivative)-inspired regulation mechanism mitigates gradient conflicts during optimization. Experiments on three large-scale urban datasets show that PRISM achieves competitive performance compared with strong multi-view baselines, while providing more stable optimization behavior and more balanced region representations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对城市多视图表示学习中静态融合与训练目标梯度失衡的问题，提出 PRISM：用稀疏 MoE 路由按区域自适应分配各视图权重，并以 PID 式调节机制缓解梯度冲突。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按样本/区域动态调节模态权重的路由，以及多目标梯度冲突的调控手段，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与推理/重构等多损失平衡提供可核查的训练与融合线索，但无视觉推理或 latent 状态内容。
